## 3. How p5.js Is Loaded in the WebViews

**p5 is bundled inline as a string — NOT loaded from CDN at runtime.** This is critical for the design decision.

**`src/utils/p5Version.ts`** (2 lines, gitignored, auto-generated):
```ts
// AUTO-GENERATED by scripts/bundle-p5.mjs — do not edit directly.
export const p5Version = "2.3.1";
```

**`src/utils/p5Source.ts`** (13 lines, gitignored, auto-generated): Contains the **entire minified p5.js library as an array of string chunks** joined into `p5Source`:
```ts
const _p = [ "...200KB chunk...", "...200KB chunk...", ... ];
export const p5Source: string = _p.join("");
```

**How it's generated — `scripts/bundle-p5.mjs`** (109 lines):
- `getLatestVersion()` (lines 43-48) fetches `https://registry.npmjs.org/p5/latest` and reads `data.version` → currently `2.3.1`.
- Constructs URL `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/p5@${version}/lib/p5.min.js` (line 94), fetches it at **build time** (lines 95-96).
- Chunks the source into 200,000-char pieces (line 64) and writes `p5Source.ts` (lines 72-82) and `p5Version.ts` (lines 84-89).
- Runs on `postinstall` and on every `npm start` (package.json lines 6-7). So the app **always bundles the newest p5.js**.

**Injection:** `exampleHtml.ts` line 46 inlines the full library into the HTML string as `<script>${p5Source}<\/script>`. The editor WebView in `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx` (line 903) does the same via `source={{ html: exerciseHtml }}`.

**Implication for your feature:** A per-module WebView would also inline `p5Source` (~1.2 MB of JS string) into each WebView's HTML. That string is already in the JS bundle (loaded once), but each WebView parses/executes its own copy of p5 in its own JS context. 16 simultaneous p5 instances is heavy.

## 5. Performance: 16 Simultaneous WebViews in a FlatList

**FlatList config in `src/app/learn/index.tsx` (lines 84-129):** There is **NO performance configuration at all**. Confirmed by grep — the only `getItemLayout` in the codebase is in `AchievementBadgeModal.tsx` line 91 (a different list). The learn FlatList uses React Native defaults:
- `initialNumToRender` = 10
- `maxToRenderPerBatch` = 10
- `windowSize` = 21 (renders ~10 items above + below viewport)
- `removeClippedSubviews` = false
- No `getItemLayout` (so all items are measured dynamically — incompatible with `getItemLayout` anyway since cards have variable text height)

The list renders 16 items total, ordered active-first (lines 75-79). With default `windowSize=21`, **all 16 cards effectively stay mounted** the moment you scroll once, because the window covers the entire short list.

**Existing multiple-WebView patterns:**
- `src/app/ref/index.tsx` lines 164-172 — renders one WebView **per example** in the reference modal. A reference entry can have several examples, so 3-5 WebViews on screen is normal there. Each runs its own p5 instance.
- `src/components/SearchOverlay.tsx` line 229 — one WebView for the previewed example.
- `src/app/learn/[course]/[id].tsx` lines 901 + 926 — one editor WebView + one fullscreen WebView (not simultaneous).
- `src/app/settings/about.tsx` line 84 — one static WebView.

**Feasibility assessment for 16 simultaneous WebViews:**
- Each WebView is a separate native process/thread with its own JS engine. Each would parse ~1.2 MB of p5 source and run a `requestAnimationFrame` loop.
- 16 concurrent rAF loops + 16 p5 instances is **very heavy** on memory and CPU. On lower-end Android devices this would likely cause jank, high memory pressure, and battery drain.
- **FlatList recycling is fundamentally incompatible with WebViews.** WebViews are expensive native views that don't mount/unmount cleanly during scroll recycling — they'd tear down and reload the p5 bundle on every recycle (causing flicker and CPU spikes), or you'd disable recycling and keep all 16 alive. There is no good middle ground.
- `react-native-webview` (v13.16.0, package.json line 51) does not provide a lightweight "headless" or shared-context mode.

**Verdict: WebView-per-card is not recommended.** It works for 1-5 stationary WebViews (reference modal) but not 16 in a scrolling list.

## 7. Web Inspiration — Looped Generative Thumbnail Ideas

From the p5.js examples gallery (fetched) plus standard generative-art patterns, here are 3 concrete, achievable ideas that translate well to either a tiny p5 sketch OR a Reanimated-SVG loop:

1. **Color-wheel / hue-cycling ring** (inspired by the p5 example "Color Wheel" — *Small circles, each with a different color, arranged in a circular path, displaying hues across the color spectrum*). 2. **Sine-wave / unit-circle tracer** (inspired by "Sine and Cosine" — *A point on the unit circle, together with the corresponding sine and cosine values on their graphs*). A dot orbits a circle while its sine/cosine traces waveforms. Ideal for `math`, `vectors`, `time`, and `transform`. In Reanimated: one `Animated.View` rotating around center + two trailing wave paths built from interpolated points.

3. **Recursive / branching tree** (inspired by "Recursive Tree" — *A rainbow fractal tree on a black background*). A small L-system tree whose branch angles breathe via `sin(frameCount)`. Great for `custom-shapes`, `curves`, and `webgl` (as a 3D-feeling wireframe). In Reanimated: a precomputed tree of `<Line>` elements with a single shared `breath` value driving branch rotation via `useAnimatedStyle` per branch level.

Bonus, also directly relevant from the gallery: **Kaleidoscope** (mirrored motifs — good for `events`/`dom` interaction theme), **Noise texture** (drifting Perlin-field dots — `random-noise`), **Triangle Strip ring** (`shapes`/`custom-shapes`), **Snowflakes** (already implemented in SplashScreen — reuse for `time` or a generic fallback).
